svg.aria-label: claude-domore planned end-state: four OS accounts on one Mac, a deterministic supervisor, one Apple container VM per attempt, an independent grader, approvals signed with a YubiKey, a learning ladder and a parked lab.
svg.title: claude-domore: planned end-state (M1 to M5)
svg.text: One Mac, separate OS accounts. Code owns every state change and permission; models only propose work. As of 2026-09-30: no engine code yet.
on Claude Max · drafts tasks, answers
can STOP · cannot approve or cancel
the engine never runs git in your repo
Reads evidence/ only, never raw output
shows every field and the full patch
signs exactly the bytes it showed
installs the runtime folder, keys, policies
never part of the task loop
LaunchDaemon, no login · each loop starts by reconciling with what really happened

g.text: host: awake · AC if unattended · disk
nonce once · counter if key has one
codex exec · clean env, pinned paths
one VM per attempt; stop ends all
the supervisor moves repo and patch
counts only checks it saw pass
changes what it tries, not its rights

svg.text: state DB · evidence · attempt folders · raw output (kept 90 days)
own git clone = source archive, never pruned · hidden test versions
secrets/: the engine's Jev key, mode 0600, left out of backups
code checks the guard of every move

g.text: M5 adds the push and PR states. Side states:

svg.text: root-owned; no account in the task loop can change what runs
stopping a VM ends every process in it
Linux Codex, own sandbox in full mode
in a guest; the engine never reads it
allow-list; DNS only for listed names
fail closed; blocks host and private IPs
never uses a rate-limit reset credit
if V1 or V2 fails for a CLI, or its
inner sandbox cannot start in the
guest: a dedicated worker OS account

g.text: You describe a change. Claude Code drafts the task and sends it with a bundle.
Jev signals category and ambiguity (allow-listed repos). Code decides.
You approve the task in the approval account: touch + PIN on the YubiKey.
Launch checks pass (quota, budget, host, no stop). The repo goes into a VM.
Codex works. The VM is stopped. The supervisor takes the patch out itself.
The candidate runs in a grader VM. The protected checker gives the verdict.
Evidence goes to your daily account. An inbox entry goes to the approver.
You read the full patch and accept it: touch + PIN.
M2: a local commit on a task branch. M5: push and PR after one more approval.
STOP at any time from your daily account, with no signature.
Only a restart signed with touch + PIN lifts it.
learns only from outcomes that the grader checked
may change what the engine tries, never what it may do
M3 harness: A/A noise, retention and canary sets, cost per success
M4: shadow mode → paired comparison → promote, or "inconclusive"
only via a release you approve
opens only after the M5 review and your own decision
no provider login, no git keys
its controller has its own Jev key
on the real Claude and Codex
enters the ladder at its own tier
